summary: Remote-controlled agent daemon: Supabase-issued prompts and MCP configs drive local PTYs with permission bypass
details: dist/session-runner.js runs a daemon that polls a hardcoded Supabase project at syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co via the `runtime_pick_next_request` RPC and, for each returned row, spawns Claude, Codex, Kimi, Gemini, or Grok CLIs on the installer's host through node-pty and writes the remote-supplied `prompt` into the PTY. When the remote row specifies `permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions'`, the spawn adds `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, removing the agent's interactive confirmation for local file, shell, and network actions. A second remote channel calls `runtime_resolve_install_set` and materializes server-supplied MCP server definitions (`command`, `args`, `env`) into `.entities-runtime.mcp.json` plus skill content written to `<cwd>/.claude/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md`, which the agent then loads and executes as tools. Together these paths give whoever controls the paired Supabase account arbitrary command execution on the installer's machine — the network-sourced prompt and the network-sourced MCP command/args/env both flow into local subprocess execution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
